s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive proptosis with ecchymosis and subconjunctival hemorrhage
salient_findings: Intraconal lesion on orbital CT with intrinsic high-density areas
key_facts: 34-year-old woman
6 months of progressive left proptosis
Recent ecchymosis and subconjunctival hemorrhage after a sudden rise in blood pressure
Intact ocular motility
Best-corrected visual acuity of 0.9 in the left eye
Normal anterior and posterior segment examinations without optic nerve signs
Right eye anophthalmic following enucleation in 2010 for choroidal melanoma
No adjuvant therapy after enucleation
Lost to follow-up after 2 years of disease-free status
Orbital CT showed a well-defined isodense intraconal lesion
Lesion measured 2.6 × 2.5 × 2.4 mm with intrinsic high-density areas
Lesion located inferomedially between the optic nerve and inferior rectus
Lesion displacing the optic nerve and inferior rectus, scalloping the lamina papyracea
MRI demonstrated a hyperintense mass on T1-weighted images and hypointense signal on T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: Metastatic choroidal melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of choroidal melanoma in the contralateral eye

shortlist.label: Cavernous hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined isodense intraconal lesion with intrinsic high-density areas on CT

shortlist.label: Orbital varix
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion location and displacement of surrounding structures

shortlist.label: Hemangiopericytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperintense mass on T1-weighted images and hypointense signal on T2-weighted images on MRI

shortlist.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion characteristics and location are consistent with this rare tumor type

raw.rationale: The lesion's well-defined borders, isodense appearance on CT, and hyperintense signal on T1-weighted MRI images with a hypointense signal on T2-weighted images are characteristic of cavernous hemangioma, which is a common benign orbital tumor.

rejected.label: Metastatic choroidal melanoma
rejected.why: The patient's history of choroidal melanoma and the new orbital lesion could suggest metastasis, but the lesion's characteristics and the lack of systemic metastatic disease make this less likely.

rejected.label: Orbital varix
rejected.why: Orbital varices typically present with intermittent proptosis and are more likely to be associated with Valsalva maneuvers or changes in head position, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Hemangiopericytoma
rejected.why: Hemangiopericytomas can have a similar appearance to cavernous hemangiomas but are less common and might have a more aggressive behavior, which is not indicated by the provided information.

rejected.label: Solitary fibrous tumor
rejected.why: Solitary fibrous tumors are rare and can have variable imaging characteristics, but the specific features described are more typical of cavernous hemangioma.
